parts.text:
Tasting note:
Ripe blackberry and cassis lead, framed by toasty oak and firm, fine-grained tannins. Long, layered finish with graphite and dried herbs. Impressive now; will reward a decade in the cellar.

quality.description: How good is this wine, according to the note? Levels: 0 = faulty: Faulty or unpleasant - the note is mostly criticism; 1 = barely_ok: Barely acceptable - drinkable, nothing to recommend it; 2 = simple: Simple and sound - correct, plain, forgettable; 3 = everyday: Pleasant everyday wine - some appeal, little depth; 4 = good: Good - clear varietal character, well made; 5 = very_good: Very good - balanced, with something to say; 6 = excellent: Excellent - complex and structured; 7 = outstanding: Outstanding - depth and length, built to age; 8 = superb: Superb - among the best of its type; 9 = profound: Profound - the note treats it as exceptional

style.description: What is the dominant style described? Options: fruit = Fruit-forward; oak = Oak-driven; mineral = Mineral, savoury; other

ageing.description: Does the note say the wine will improve with age?
